### `cardinality`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](cardinality.md)

MEASURED cardinality. `child` is how many rows of the referencing relation relate to one row of the parent; `parent` the converse. An identity parent is `one`; a key PART is `many`, because a shared value domain is not an identifying join.

Its own keys: [`dataset.columns.references.cardinality`](cardinality.md)

### `participation`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](participation.md)

MEASURED participation — the half a key cannot supply. `parent: optional` means some parent rows are referenced by NO child row; `child: optional` means some child rows carry no parent. Without it an optional relationship and a mandatory one draw the same crow's foot wherever nobody thought about it.

Its own keys: [`dataset.columns.references.participation`](participation.md)
